messages.subject: Multichannel Sound Card Output
parts:
I am working on an experiment that utilizes a soundcard to play sound and output electrical signals from a multi-channel sound card. From MatLab, I can directly drive each channel, but I would prefer to use R. I have been able to make a multi-channel file and name the channels, but I'm unable to get them to play properly. I have set the soundcard as the default and when I play the test in the config window in the 'Sound' window, but when I run my code it does not play. The code opens WMP and a file plays that is the correct length for the signal I created, but I'm not getting sound from the speakers and I'm not able to measure an electrical signal from the other channels that I have set up. 

Windows 7
Soundcard: Lynx E44
R 3.4.4

s1 <- 10*sin(2*pi*440*seq(0,1,length.out=8000))
s1_multi <- WaveMC(data = cbind(s1, s1, s1, s1),
                   samp.rate=8000, 
                   bit=16)
colnames(s1_multi) <- c("FL", "FR", "FC", "LF")
setWavPlayer(shQuote("C:/Program Files (x86)/Windows Media Player/wmplayer.exe"))

listen(s1_multi)

Anything I'm doing wrong? Is there a way to drive the channels of the sound card directly from R?

Thanks.

messages.author: 65c82d09eac308cf
messages.subject: Re: [seewave] Multichannel Sound Card Output
parts:
Dear Jason,
The function listen() works with multi channels wav files but plays only the first channel (something I could change in a next release with an argument to set up the channel to listen to).
Using your example I could listen to the 440 Hz tone (Ubuntu 16.04, "play" player of SoX 14.4.1, Intel Corporation Device a2f0 sound card) but I have unfortunately no idea how to fix your issue.
I am sorry not to be able to help more,
Best
Jerome
